//: Descrições, argumentos e categorias das funções em inglês (o motor guarda o português). Chave das descrições: nome canônico.

descricoes.ACCRINT: Accrued interest of a security that pays periodic interest.
descricoes.ACCRINTM: Accrued interest of a security that pays interest at maturity.
descricoes.ADDRESS: Builds a cell address as text. Abs: 1 $A$1, 2 A$1, 3 $A1, 4 A1; a1 FALSE gives R1C1 style. E.g. =ADDRESS(2,3) returns $C$2.
descricoes.AGGREGATE: Aggregates with options to ignore hidden rows, errors and nested subtotals (options 0–7). Functions 1–19; 14 to 19 use k (LARGE, SMALL, PERCENTILE, QUARTILE).
descricoes.AMORDEGRC: Depreciation for each period in the French system, with a coefficient by useful life.
descricoes.AMORLINC: Straight-line depreciation for each period in the French system (prorated first period).
descricoes.AND: True only if all are true.
descricoes.ARABIC: Converts Roman numerals to a number.
descricoes.AREAS: Number of areas in the reference.
descricoes.ARRAYTOTEXT: Converts an array to text; with format 1, in strict array style.
descricoes.ASC: Changes full-width letters, digits and symbols to half-width.
descricoes.ATAN2: Arctangent of the x and y coordinates, in radians.
descricoes.AVEDEV: Mean absolute deviation from the mean.
descricoes.AVERAGEA: Average, counting text as 0 and TRUE as 1.
descricoes.AVERAGEIF: Average of the cells that meet the criteria.
descricoes.AVERAGEIFS: Average of the rows that meet all criteria.
descricoes.BAHTTEXT: The amount in baht spelled out in Thai.
descricoes.BASE: Writes a number in another base, with leading zeros.
descricoes.BESSELI: Modified Bessel function In(x). E.g. =BESSELI(1.5,1) returns 0.981666.
descricoes.BESSELJ: Bessel function of the first kind Jn(x). E.g. =BESSELJ(1.9,2) returns 0.329926.
descricoes.BESSELK: Modified Bessel function of the second kind Kn(x), x > 0. E.g. =BESSELK(1.5,1) gives 0.277388.
descricoes.BESSELY: Bessel function of the second kind Yn(x), x > 0. E.g. =BESSELY(2.5,1) gives 0.145918.
descricoes.BETA.DIST: Beta distribution: density or cumulative probability.
descricoes.BETA.INV: Inverse of the cumulative beta distribution.
descricoes.BETAINV: Inverse of the cumulative beta distribution. (compatibility)
descricoes.BIN2DEC: Converts a binary number to decimal.
descricoes.BIN2HEX: Converts a binary number to hexadecimal.
descricoes.BIN2OCT: Converts a binary number to octal.
descricoes.BINOM.DIST.RANGE: Probability that the number of successes falls in a range.
descricoes.BINOM.INV: Smallest number of successes whose cumulative binomial probability reaches alpha.
descricoes.BITAND: Bitwise AND of two non-negative integers.
descricoes.BITLSHIFT: Shifts the bits of a number to the left.
descricoes.BITOR: Bitwise OR of two non-negative integers.
descricoes.BITRSHIFT: Shifts the bits of a number to the right.
descricoes.BITXOR: Bitwise exclusive OR of two non-negative integers.
descricoes.BYCOL: Applies the LAMBDA (or a function name) to each column and returns a row. E.g. =BYCOL(A1:C3,MAX).
descricoes.BYROW: Applies the LAMBDA (or a function name) to each row and returns a column. E.g. =BYROW(A1:C3,LAMBDA(r,SUM(r))).
descricoes.CALL: Recognized so Excel files open; returns #N/A, because it needs a server, a DLL or an internet service, and FeatherSheet runs everything on the computer.
descricoes.CEILING.MATH: Rounds up to the nearest integer or multiple.
descricoes.CEILING.PRECISE: Rounds up, toward plus infinity, to a multiple.
descricoes.CELL: Information about the cell: "address", "col", "row", "contents", "type" (b blank, l text, v value), "prefix", "format", "width", "protect".
descricoes.CHIINV: Inverse of the right-tailed chi-squared distribution. (compatibility)
descricoes.CHISQ.INV: Inverse of the left-tailed chi-squared distribution.
descricoes.CHISQ.INV.RT: Inverse of the right-tailed chi-squared distribution.
descricoes.CHISQ.TEST: Returns the probability of the chi-squared test of independence.
descricoes.CHITEST: Old name of CHISQ.TEST: probability of the chi-squared test of independence.
descricoes.CHOOSE: Chooses a value from the list by index.
descricoes.CHOOSECOLS: Returns only the given columns, in the requested order; negative counts from the last. E.g. =CHOOSECOLS(A1:D5,1,3).
descricoes.CHOOSEROWS: Returns only the given rows, in the requested order; negative counts from the last. E.g. =CHOOSEROWS(A1:D5,1,-1).
descricoes.CLEAN: Removes non-printable control characters from the text.
descricoes.CODE: Windows-1252 code of the first character.
descricoes.COLUMNS: Number of columns in the range.
descricoes.COMPLEX: Builds a complex number as text a+bi, with suffix i (default) or j. E.g. =COMPLEX(3,4) returns 3+4i.
descricoes.CONCATENATE: Joins the arguments into one text (old function: does not accept a range; use CONCAT).
descricoes.CONFIDENCE: Half-width of the confidence interval using the normal distribution. (compatibility)
descricoes.CONFIDENCE.NORM: Half-width of the confidence interval using the normal distribution.
descricoes.CONFIDENCE.T: Half-width of the confidence interval using Student's t distribution.
descricoes.CONVERT: Converts between units of measure (mass, distance, time, pressure, force, energy, power, temperature, volume, area, speed, information). E.g. =CONVERT(1,"mi","km") returns 1.609344.
descricoes.CORREL: Correlation between the two sets, from -1 to 1.
descricoes.COS: Cosine of an angle in radians.
descricoes.COT: Cotangent of an angle in radians.
descricoes.COUNT: Counts how many cells contain numbers.
descricoes.COUNTA: Counts the cells that are not empty.
descricoes.COUNTBLANK: Counts the empty cells in the range.
descricoes.COUNTBYCOLOR: Counts the cells with content in the range whose color is that of the sample cell (or a "#RRGGBB" text). Type 0 (default) compares the fill; 1, the font color. Does not see conditional formatting. Does not exist in Excel.
descricoes.COUNTIF: Counts the cells that meet the criteria.
descricoes.COUNTIFS: Counts the rows that meet all criteria.
descricoes.COUNTUNIQUE: How many different values there are.
descricoes.COUPDAYBS: Days from the start of the coupon period to settlement.
descricoes.COUPDAYS: Days in the coupon period that contains settlement.
descricoes.COUPDAYSNC: Days from settlement to the next coupon date.
descricoes.COUPNUM: Number of coupons payable between settlement and maturity.
descricoes.COVARIANCE.P: Population covariance of pairs of values.
descricoes.COVARIANCE.S: Sample covariance of pairs of values.
descricoes.CRITBINOM: Smallest number of successes whose cumulative binomial probability reaches alpha. (compatibility)
descricoes.CSC: Cosecant of an angle in radians.
descricoes.CUBEKPIMEMBER: Recognized so Excel files open; returns #N/A, because it needs a server, a DLL or an internet service, and FeatherSheet runs everything on the computer.
descricoes.CUBEMEMBER: Recognized so Excel files open; returns #N/A, because it needs a server, a DLL or an internet service, and FeatherSheet runs everything on the computer.
descricoes.CUBEMEMBERPROPERTY: Recognized so Excel files open; returns #N/A, because it needs a server, a DLL or an internet service, and FeatherSheet runs everything on the computer.
descricoes.CUBERANKEDMEMBER: Recognized so Excel files open; returns #N/A, because it needs a server, a DLL or an internet service, and FeatherSheet runs everything on the computer.
descricoes.CUBESET: Recognized so Excel files open; returns #N/A, because it needs a server, a DLL or an internet service, and FeatherSheet runs everything on the computer.
descricoes.CUBESETCOUNT: Recognized so Excel files open; returns #N/A, because it needs a server, a DLL or an internet service, and FeatherSheet runs everything on the computer.
descricoes.CUBEVALUE: Recognized so Excel files open; returns #N/A, because it needs a server, a DLL or an internet service, and FeatherSheet runs everything on the computer.
descricoes.CUMIPMT: Cumulative interest paid between two periods.
descricoes.CUMPRINC: Cumulative principal paid between two periods.
descricoes.DATE: Builds a date from its parts.
descricoes.DATEDIF: Difference between two dates. Unit: "Y" years, "M" months, "D" days, "YM" months left over in the year, "YD" days left over in the year, "MD" days left over in the month.
descricoes.DATEVALUE: Converts a date written as text (dd/mm/yyyy) to a serial number.
descricoes.DAVERAGE: Average of the numbers of a field in the records that meet the criteria.
descricoes.DAY: Day of the month of a date.
descricoes.DAYS: Returns the number of days between two dates.
descricoes.DAYS360: Counts the days between two dates in a 360-day year (US or European method).
descricoes.DB: Fixed-declining balance depreciation for a period.
descricoes.DBCS: Changes half-width letters, digits and symbols to full-width.
descricoes.DCOUNT: Counts the numeric cells of a field in the records that meet the criteria.
descricoes.DCOUNTA: Counts the non-empty cells of a field in the records that meet the criteria.
descricoes.DDB: Double-declining balance (or another factor) depreciation for a period.
descricoes.DEC2BIN: Converts a decimal number to binary.
descricoes.DEC2HEX: Converts a decimal number to hexadecimal.
descricoes.DEC2OCT: Converts a decimal number to octal.
descricoes.DECIMAL: Reads a text in a given base and returns the number.
descricoes.DELTA: Returns 1 when the two numbers are equal, otherwise 0.
descricoes.DETECTLANGUAGE: Recognized so Excel files open; returns #N/A, because it needs a server, a DLL or an internet service, and FeatherSheet runs everything on the computer.
descricoes.DEVSQ: Sum of the squares of the deviations.
descricoes.DGET: Returns the field value of the single record that meets the criteria.
descricoes.DISC: Discount rate of a security. E.g. =DISC(DATE(2018,1,25),DATE(2018,6,15),97.975,100,1) returns 5.24%.
descricoes.DMAX: Largest number of a field in the records that meet the criteria.
descricoes.DMIN: Smallest number of a field in the records that meet the criteria.
descricoes.DOLLAR: Formats the number as currency text (R$).
descricoes.DOLLARDE: Converts a price in fractional notation to a decimal number.
descricoes.DOLLARFR: Converts a decimal price to fractional notation.
descricoes.DPRODUCT: Multiplies the numbers of a field in the records that meet the criteria.
descricoes.DROP: Drops the first (positive) or last (negative) rows and columns of the array. E.g. =DROP(A1:C5,1) removes the first row.
descricoes.DSTDEV: Sample standard deviation of a field in the records that meet the criteria.
descricoes.DSTDEVP: Population standard deviation of a field in the records that meet the criteria.
descricoes.DSUM: Adds the numbers of a field in the records that meet the criteria.
descricoes.DURATION: Macaulay duration of a coupon bond, in years.
descricoes.DVAR: Sample variance of a field in the records that meet the criteria.
descricoes.DVARP: Population variance of a field in the records that meet the criteria.
descricoes.EDATE: Adds or subtracts months from a date.
descricoes.EFFECT: Effective annual rate from a nominal rate and compounding periods.
descricoes.ENCODEURL: Encodes the text for use in a web address (UTF-8, %XX). E.g. =ENCODEURL("a b") returns a%20b.
descricoes.EOMONTH: Returns the date of the last day of the month.
descricoes.ERF: Error function integrated from 0 to a limit, or between two limits.
descricoes.ERF.PRECISE: Error function integrated from 0 to x.
descricoes.ERROR.TYPE: Number that identifies the error type (1 to 9); #N/A if it is not an error.
descricoes.EUROCONVERT: Converts between the euro and the former euro-area currencies at the fixed rates ("DEM", "FRF", "PTE"…).
descricoes.EVEN: Rounds up, away from zero, to the nearest even integer.
descricoes.EXACT: TRUE when the two texts are equal, including case.
descricoes.EXPAND: Expands the array to the requested size, filling the new space (default #N/A). E.g. =EXPAND(A1:B2,3,3,0).
descricoes.EXPON.DIST: Exponential distribution: density or cumulative probability.
descricoes.EXPONDIST: Exponential distribution: density or cumulative probability. (compatibility)
descricoes.F.DIST: F distribution: density or left-tailed probability.
descricoes.F.INV: Inverse of the left-tailed F distribution.
descricoes.F.INV.RT: Inverse of the right-tailed F distribution.
descricoes.F.TEST: Two-tailed F-test: probability that the variances of the two arrays are not different. E.g. =F.TEST(A1:A5,B1:B5).
descricoes.FETCHTEXT: Returns the content of an address as raw text, without parsing.
descricoes.FILTER: Returns only the rows (or columns) where the condition is true. The result spills into the neighboring cells.
descricoes.FILTERXML: Values from XML text by an XPath (/a/b, //b, [1], [@id='x'], /@attribute, text()). E.g. =FILTERXML(A1,"//item").
descricoes.FIND: Position of the text, case-sensitive and without wildcards.
descricoes.FINDB: Position of a text within another (case-sensitive); in single-byte languages it equals FIND.
descricoes.FINV: Inverse of the right-tailed F distribution. (compatibility)
descricoes.FIXED: Rounds the number and returns it as text with decimal places and a thousands separator.
descricoes.FLOOR.MATH: Rounds down to the nearest integer or multiple.
descricoes.FLOOR.PRECISE: Rounds down, toward minus infinity, to a multiple.
descricoes.FORECAST: Projects a value using the trend line.
descricoes.FORECAST.ETS: Forecast by triple exponential smoothing (additive trend and seasonality). Seasonality 1 detects it, 0 turns it off.
descricoes.FORECAST.ETS.CONFINT: Half-width of the FORECAST.ETS confidence interval at the target date (95% by default).
descricoes.FORECAST.ETS.SEASONALITY: Length of the season FORECAST.ETS detects (0 = no seasonality).
descricoes.FORECAST.ETS.STAT: Statistic of the FORECAST.ETS model: 1 alpha, 2 beta, 3 gamma, 4 MASE, 5 SMAPE, 6 MAE, 7 RMSE, 8 step size.
descricoes.FORECAST.LINEAR: Projects a value using the trend line.
descricoes.FORMULATEXT: Text of the cell's formula; #N/A if it has none.
descricoes.FREQUENCY: How many data points fall in each bin. Spills a column with one row more than the bins: the last counts what is above the highest limit.
descricoes.FV: Future value of an investment with constant payments and rate.
descricoes.FVSCHEDULE: Future value of a principal after a series of compound interest rates.
descricoes.GAMMA.DIST: Gamma distribution: density or cumulative probability.
descricoes.GAMMA.INV: Inverse of the cumulative gamma distribution.
descricoes.GAMMADIST: Gamma distribution: density or cumulative probability. (compatibility)
descricoes.GAMMAINV: Inverse of the cumulative gamma distribution. (compatibility)
descricoes.GAMMALN: Natural logarithm of the gamma function.
descricoes.GAMMALN.PRECISE: Natural logarithm of the gamma function.
descricoes.GAUSS: Probability that a standard normal value falls between the mean and z.
descricoes.GCD: Greatest common divisor of the numbers.
descricoes.GEOMEAN: Geometric mean; useful for growth rates.
descricoes.GESTEP: Returns 1 when the number is greater than or equal to the step, otherwise 0.
descricoes.GETPIVOTDATA: Value from a pivot table on the sheet: the data field, a cell of the table and field/item pairs. With no pairs, the Grand Total.
descricoes.GROUPBY: Groups the values by the fields and applies the function to each group, with a total. E.g. =GROUPBY(A2:A9,C2:C9,SUM).
descricoes.GROWTH: Values along the exponential growth curve y = b·m^x for the new x values. Accepts one x variable.
descricoes.HARMEAN: Harmonic mean; useful for average speeds.
descricoes.HEX2BIN: Converts a hexadecimal number to binary.
descricoes.HEX2DEC: Converts a hexadecimal number to decimal.
descricoes.HEX2OCT: Converts a hexadecimal number to octal.
descricoes.HLOOKUP: Looks in the first row and returns the value of the given row.
descricoes.HOUR: Returns the hour (0 to 23) of a time.
descricoes.HSTACK: Joins arrays horizontally, side by side; missing height becomes #N/A. E.g. =HSTACK(A1:A3,C1:C3).
descricoes.HYPERLINK: Shows the friendly name (or the address itself) as a link. E.g. =HYPERLINK("https://example.com","Open").
descricoes.HYPGEOMDIST: Hypergeometric probability of an exact count (compatibility).
descricoes.IF: Returns one value or another according to the test.
descricoes.IFERROR: Replaces the result when it is an error.
descricoes.IFNA: Returns value_if_na if the result is #N/A.
descricoes.IFS: Tests conditions in order and returns the one of the first true.
descricoes.IMABS: Absolute value of a complex number. E.g. =IMABS("3+4i") returns 5.
descricoes.IMAGE: Shows in the cell the image stored in base64 (or in a data URL).
descricoes.IMAGE.BASE64: The plain base64 of an image (from the cell with IMAGE or from a data URL).
descricoes.IMAGINARY: Imaginary part of a complex number. E.g. =IMAGINARY("3+4i") returns 4.
descricoes.IMARGUMENT: Angle, in radians, of the complex number in the complex plane. Zero gives #DIV/0!. E.g. =IMARGUMENT("i") returns 1.5707963267949.
descricoes.IMCONJUGATE: Conjugate of a complex number (flips the sign of the imaginary part). E.g. =IMCONJUGATE("3+4i") returns 3-4i.
descricoes.IMCOS: Cosine of a complex number. E.g. =IMCOS("0") returns 1.
descricoes.IMCOSH: Hyperbolic cosine of a complex number. E.g. =IMCOSH("0") returns 1.
descricoes.IMCOT: Cotangent of a complex number (cosine over sine). A zero sine gives #NUM!. E.g. =IMCOT("1+i").
descricoes.IMCSC: Cosecant of a complex number. E.g. =IMCSC("1+i"). A zero sine gives #NUM!.
descricoes.IMCSCH: Hyperbolic cosecant of a complex number. E.g. =IMCSCH("1+i"). A zero hyperbolic sine gives #NUM!.
descricoes.IMDIV: Quotient of two complex numbers. A zero divisor gives #NUM!. E.g. =IMDIV("-238+240i","10+24i") returns 5+12i.
descricoes.IMEXP: Exponential of a complex number. E.g. =IMEXP("0") returns 1.
descricoes.IMLN: Natural logarithm of a complex number. Zero gives #NUM!. E.g. =IMLN("1") returns 0.
descricoes.IMLOG10: Base-10 logarithm of a complex number. Zero gives #NUM!. E.g. =IMLOG10("10") returns 1.
descricoes.IMLOG2: Base-2 logarithm of a complex number. Zero gives #NUM!. E.g. =IMLOG2("8") returns 3.
descricoes.IMPORTDATA: Reads a CSV or TSV from an internet address and spills the table into the grid. The separator is detected automatically, or give ";" as the second argument.
descricoes.IMPORTJSON: Reads a JSON from an address and brings back a piece of it. The path uses dots and brackets: "dados.itens[0].nome". A list of objects becomes a table with a header.
descricoes.IMPOWER: Raises a complex number to a power. E.g. =IMPOWER("2+3i",3) returns -46+9i.
descricoes.IMPRODUCT: Multiplies all the given complex numbers. E.g. =IMPRODUCT("3+4i","5-3i") returns 27+11i.
descricoes.IMREAL: Real part of a complex number. E.g. =IMREAL("3+4i") returns 3.
descricoes.IMSEC: Secant of a complex number. E.g. =IMSEC("0") returns 1.
descricoes.IMSECH: Hyperbolic secant of a complex number. E.g. =IMSECH("0") returns 1.
descricoes.IMSIN: Sine of a complex number. E.g. =IMSIN("0") returns 0.
descricoes.IMSINH: Hyperbolic sine of a complex number. E.g. =IMSINH("0") returns 0.
descricoes.IMSQRT: Principal square root of a complex number. E.g. =IMSQRT("-4") returns 2i.
descricoes.IMSUB: Difference between two complex numbers. E.g. =IMSUB("13+4i","5+3i") returns 8+i.
descricoes.IMSUM: Adds the given complex numbers, including ranges. E.g. =IMSUM("3+4i","5-3i") returns 8+i.
descricoes.IMTAN: Tangent of a complex number. E.g. =IMTAN("0") returns 0.
descricoes.INDEX: Value at the given position within the range.
descricoes.INDIRECT: Reference given as text ("B7", "Data!A1:C9" or a name); a1 FALSE reads R1C1 style. E.g. =INDIRECT("A"&B1).
descricoes.INT: Rounds down to the nearest integer.
descricoes.INTERCEPT: Where that line crosses the vertical axis.
descricoes.INTRATE: Interest rate of a fully invested security.
descricoes.IPMT: Interest part of the payment for a given period.
descricoes.IRR: Internal rate of return of periodic cash flows.
descricoes.ISBLANK: True if the cell is empty.
descricoes.ISERR: True if the value is any error except #N/A.
descricoes.ISERROR: True if the value is an error.
descricoes.ISEVEN: TRUE when the number is even.
descricoes.ISFORMULA: TRUE if the cell holds a formula.
descricoes.ISLOGICAL: True if the value is TRUE or FALSE.
descricoes.ISNA: True if the value is the #N/A error.
descricoes.ISNONTEXT: True if the value is not text (including empty).
descricoes.ISNUMBER: True if the value is a number.
descricoes.ISO.CEILING: Rounds up, toward plus infinity, to a multiple (ISO).
descricoes.ISODD: TRUE when the number is odd.
descricoes.ISOMITTED: Inside a LAMBDA, TRUE if the parameter was not passed.
descricoes.ISOWEEKNUM: Returns the ISO 8601 week number of a date.
descricoes.ISPMT: Interest paid in a period of a loan with constant principal repayment.
descricoes.ISREF: TRUE if the argument is a cell or range reference. E.g. =ISREF(A1) returns TRUE.
descricoes.ISTEXT: True if the value is text.
descricoes.KURT: Kurtosis: how peaked the distribution is.
descricoes.LCM: Least common multiple of the numbers.
descricoes.LEFTB: First bytes of the text; in single-byte languages it equals LEFT.
descricoes.LENB: Number of bytes in the text; in single-byte languages it equals LEN.
descricoes.LET: Defines local variables to use in the formula.
descricoes.LINEST: Least-squares linear regression (one or more variables): coefficients mₙ…m₁ and b; with stats, also standard errors, R², F and sums of squares.
descricoes.LOGEST: Exponential curve y = b·m₁^x₁·…: returns mₙ…m₁ and b (and the statistics, on the log scale).
descricoes.LOGINV: Inverse of the cumulative lognormal distribution. (compatibility)
descricoes.LOGNORM.DIST: Lognormal distribution: density or cumulative probability.
descricoes.LOGNORM.INV: Inverse of the cumulative lognormal distribution.
descricoes.LOOKUP: Looks up the value in a vector in ascending order and returns the matching item of the result vector (approximate). E.g. =LOOKUP(5,A1:A9,B1:B9).
descricoes.MAKEARRAY: Builds an array by calling LAMBDA(row, col) at each position. E.g. =MAKEARRAY(3,3,LAMBDA(r,c,r*c)).
descricoes.MAP: Applies the lambda function to each element of the array.
descricoes.MATCH: Position of the value within the range. Use 0 for exact.
descricoes.MAXA: Largest value, counting text as 0 and TRUE as 1.
descricoes.MAXIFS: Largest value among the rows that meet the criteria.
descricoes.MEDIAN: Middle value of the sorted set.
descricoes.MID: Part of the text from a position.
descricoes.MIDB: Middle bytes of the text; in single-byte languages it equals MID.
descricoes.MINA: Smallest value, counting text as 0 and TRUE as 1.
descricoes.MINIFS: Smallest value among the rows that meet the criteria.
descricoes.MINUTE: Returns the minute (0 to 59) of a time.
descricoes.MINVERSE: Inverse matrix of a square matrix.
descricoes.MIRR: Modified internal rate of return, with finance cost and reinvestment rate.
descricoes.MMULT: Product of two matrices. The columns of the first must match the rows of the second.
descricoes.MODE.MULT: Vertical array with all the modes (most frequent values).
descricoes.MODE.SNGL: Same as MODE. Most frequent value.
descricoes.MULTINOMIAL: Ratio of the factorial of a sum to the product of the factorials.
descricoes.MUNIT: Identity matrix of the given dimension.
descricoes.N: Converts the value to a number: a number stays, TRUE becomes 1, the rest becomes 0.
descricoes.NA: Returns the #N/A error (value not available). E.g. =IF(A1="",NA(),A1).
descricoes.NETWORKDAYS: Counts the working days between two dates.
descricoes.NETWORKDAYS.INTL: Counts the working days between two dates, with customizable weekends.
descricoes.NOMINAL: Nominal annual rate from an effective rate and compounding periods.
descricoes.NORM.INV: Inverse of the normal distribution for the probability.
descricoes.NORM.S.DIST: Standard normal distribution (mean 0 and standard deviation 1).
descricoes.NORM.S.INV: Inverse of the cumulative standard normal distribution.
descricoes.NORMDIST: Same as NORM.DIST. Normal distribution (density or cumulative).
descricoes.NORMINV: Same as NORM.INV. Inverse of the normal distribution for the probability.
descricoes.NORMSINV: Inverse of the cumulative standard normal distribution. (compatibility)
descricoes.NPER: Number of periods needed to pay off or accumulate an amount.
descricoes.NPV: Net present value of periodic cash flows at a discount rate.
descricoes.NUMBERVALUE: Converts text to a number, with chosen separators (pt-BR default: decimal comma, thousands period).
descricoes.OCT2BIN: Converts an octal number to binary.
descricoes.OCT2DEC: Converts an octal number to decimal.
descricoes.OCT2HEX: Converts an octal number to hexadecimal.
descricoes.ODD: Rounds up, away from zero, to the nearest odd integer.
descricoes.ODDFPRICE: Price per 100 of a security with an odd first period.
descricoes.ODDFYIELD: Yield of a security with an odd first period.
descricoes.ODDLPRICE: Price per 100 of a security with an odd last period.
descricoes.ODDLYIELD: Yield of a security with an odd last period.
descricoes.OFFSET: Reference shifted by rows and columns from ref, with the given height and width. E.g. =SUM(OFFSET(A1,0,0,3)) sums A1:A3.
descricoes.OR: True if at least one is true.
descricoes.PDURATION: Periods needed for an investment to grow to the target value.
descricoes.PERCENTILE: Value below which fraction p of the data lies (p between 0 and 1).
descricoes.PERCENTILE.EXC: k-th percentile, with k strictly between 0 and 1.
descricoes.PERCENTILE.INC: Same as PERCENTILE. Value below which fraction p of the data lies (p between 0 and 1).
descricoes.PERCENTOF: Sum of the subset divided by the sum of the total (fraction of the total). A zero total gives #DIV/0!.
descricoes.PERCENTRANK: Same as PERCENTRANK.INC. Relative rank of a value, from 0 to 1 inclusive.
descricoes.PERCENTRANK.EXC: Relative rank of a value, strictly between 0 and 1.
descricoes.PERCENTRANK.INC: Relative rank of a value, from 0 to 1 inclusive.
descricoes.PERMUT: How many arrangements, taking order into account.
descricoes.PHI: Density of the standard normal distribution.
descricoes.PHONETIC: Phonetic text (furigana) of the cell; without it, the text itself.
descricoes.PIVOTBY: Cross tab: rows by one field, columns by another, the function at each crossing and the totals. E.g. =PIVOTBY(A2:A9,B2:B9,C2:C9,SUM).
descricoes.PMT: Periodic payment of a loan or annuity, with constant payments and rate.
descricoes.PPMT: Principal part of the payment for a given period.
descricoes.PRICE: Price per 100 face value of a security that pays periodic interest. E.g. =PRICE(DATE(2008,2,15),DATE(2017,11,15),5.75%,6.5%,100,2) gives 94.63.
descricoes.PRICEDISC: Price per $100 face value of a discounted security.
descricoes.PRICEMAT: Price per $100 of a security that pays interest at maturity.
descricoes.PROB: Probability that the x values fall between the limits (or equal the lower limit). The probabilities must add up to 1.
descricoes.PROPER: Capitalizes the first letter of each word.
descricoes.PV: Present value of a series of equal future payments.
descricoes.QUARTILE.EXC: Quartile (1 to 3) of a data set, by the exclusive method.
descricoes.QUARTILE.INC: Same as QUARTILE. Quartile: 0 minimum, 1, 2 median, 3, 4 maximum.
descricoes.RAND: Random number between 0 and 1. Recalculates on every change.
descricoes.RANDARRAY: Array of random numbers; with integer TRUE it draws whole numbers between min and max. E.g. =RANDARRAY(3,2,1,10,TRUE).
descricoes.RANK: Position of the value in the sorted list.
descricoes.RANK.AVG: Rank of a number in the list; ties get the average rank.
descricoes.RANK.EQ: Rank of a number in the list; ties get the highest rank.
descricoes.RATE: Interest rate per period of an annuity.
descricoes.RECEIVED: Amount received at maturity of a fully invested security.
descricoes.REDUCE: Reduces the array to an accumulated value using lambda.
descricoes.REGEXEXTRACT: Extracts the part that matches the regular expression.
descricoes.REGEXMATCH: TRUE if the text matches the regular expression.
descricoes.REGEXREPLACE: Replaces the pattern found by the regular expression.
descricoes.REGEXTEST: TRUE when the regular expression finds a match in the text.
descricoes.REGISTER.ID: Recognized so Excel files open; returns #N/A, because it needs a server, a DLL or an internet service, and FeatherSheet runs everything on the computer.
descricoes.REPLACE: Replaces part of the text by position.
descricoes.REPLACEB: Replaces part of the text with another; in single-byte languages it equals REPLACE.
descricoes.RIGHTB: Last bytes of the text; in single-byte languages it equals RIGHT.
descricoes.ROMAN: Converts a number to Roman numerals (text).
descricoes.ROUND: Rounds to the number of decimal places.
descricoes.ROWS: Number of rows in the range.
descricoes.RRI: Equivalent interest rate for the growth of an investment.
descricoes.RSQ: R²: how much the line explains the data.
descricoes.RTD: Recognized so Excel files open; returns #N/A, because it needs a server, a DLL or an internet service, and FeatherSheet runs everything on the computer.
descricoes.SCAN: Like REDUCE, but returns every step of the accumulator. E.g. =SCAN(0,A1:A5,LAMBDA(a,v,a+v)) gives the running total.
descricoes.SEARCH: Position of the text, ignoring case; accepts ? and * as wildcards.
descricoes.SEARCHB: Position of a text within another (accepts wildcards, ignores case); in single-byte languages it equals SEARCH.
descricoes.SEC: Secant of an angle in radians.
descricoes.SECOND: Returns the second (0 to 59) of a time.
descricoes.SHEET: Sheet number (1 = first tab) of the reference, of a sheet name given as text or, with no argument, of the formula's sheet.
descricoes.SHEETS: Number of sheets in the workbook (no argument) or in the reference.
descricoes.SIGN: Returns -1, 0 or 1 according to the sign.
descricoes.SIN: Sine of an angle in radians.
descricoes.SLOPE: Slope of the line that best describes the points.
descricoes.SORT: Sorts the rows of the range by one column.
descricoes.SORTBY: Sorts the array by the values of another array. Order: 1 ascending (default), -1 descending. E.g. =SORTBY(A2:B9,B2:B9,-1).
descricoes.STDEV.P: Standard deviation of the whole population.
descricoes.STDEV.S: Same as STDEV. Standard deviation of a sample.
descricoes.STDEVA: Sample standard deviation, counting text as 0 and logicals as 1/0.
descricoes.STDEVP: Same as STDEV.P. Standard deviation of the whole population.
descricoes.STDEVPA: Population standard deviation, counting text as 0 and logicals as 1/0.
descricoes.STEYX: Standard error of the predicted y value for each x in the linear regression. Needs 3 or more pairs.
descricoes.STOCKHISTORY: Recognized so Excel files open; returns #N/A, because it needs a server, a DLL or an internet service, and FeatherSheet runs everything on the computer.
descricoes.SUBSTITUTE: Replaces one piece of text with another.
descricoes.SUBTOTAL: Subtotal of a range ignoring nested subtotals and hidden rows (101–111 and 1–11; hidden or filtered rows are left out). 9/109 sum, 1/101 average, 2/102 count numbers, 3/103 count values, 4/104 max, 5/105 min, 7/107 standard deviation, 10/110 variance.
descricoes.SUM: Adds the given numbers or ranges.
descricoes.SUMBYCOLOR: Adds the numbers in the range whose color is that of the sample cell (or a "#RRGGBB" text). Type 0 (default) compares the fill; 1, the font color. Does not see conditional formatting. Does not exist in Excel.
descricoes.SUMIF: Adds only the cells that meet the criteria.
descricoes.SUMIFS: Adds when all criteria match at the same time.
descricoes.SUMPRODUCT: Multiplies the arrays item by item and adds the products.
descricoes.SUMSQ: Sum of the squares of the numbers.
descricoes.SUMX2MY2: Sum of the differences of squares of corresponding elements.
descricoes.SUMX2PY2: Sum of the sums of squares of corresponding elements.
descricoes.SUMXMY2: Sum of the squares of the differences of corresponding elements.
descricoes.SWITCH: Compares the expression with options and returns the value of the matching case.
descricoes.T: Returns the value if it is text; otherwise, empty text.
descricoes.T.INV: Inverse of the left-tailed Student's t distribution.
descricoes.T.INV.2T: Inverse of the two-tailed Student's t distribution.
descricoes.T.TEST: Returns the probability associated with Student's t-test.
descricoes.TAKE: Returns the first (positive) or last (negative) rows and columns of the array. E.g. =TAKE(A1:C5,2) returns the first 2 rows.
descricoes.TAN: Tangent of an angle in radians.
descricoes.TBILLEQ: Bond-equivalent yield of a Treasury bill.
descricoes.TBILLPRICE: Price per $100 of a Treasury bill (maturity within one year).
descricoes.TDIST: Student's t probability with one or two tails (compatibility).
descricoes.TEXTAFTER: Returns the text after the given delimiter.
descricoes.TEXTBEFORE: Returns the text before the given delimiter.
descricoes.TEXTSPLIT: Splits the text into columns and rows.
descricoes.TIME: Builds a time (fraction of the day) from hour, minute and second.
descricoes.TIMEVALUE: Converts a time written as text (hh:mm:ss) to a fraction of the day.
descricoes.TINV: Inverse of the two-tailed Student's t distribution. (compatibility)
descricoes.TOCOL: Turns the array into a single column. Ignore: 0 nothing, 1 blanks, 2 errors, 3 both. E.g. =TOCOL(A1:C3).
descricoes.TOROW: Turns the array into a single row. Ignore: 0 nothing, 1 blanks, 2 errors, 3 both. E.g. =TOROW(A1:C3).
descricoes.TRANSLATE: Recognized so Excel files open; returns #N/A, because it needs a server, a DLL or an internet service, and FeatherSheet runs everything on the computer.
descricoes.TREND: Values along the linear trend line (least squares) for the new x values. Accepts one x variable.
descricoes.TRIMMEAN: Average excluding a fraction of points at both ends.
descricoes.TRIMRANGE: The range without the empty rows and columns at its edges. 0 none, 1 leading, 2 trailing, 3 both (default). E.g. =TRIMRANGE(A:A).
descricoes.TRUNC: Cuts off the decimal places without rounding.
descricoes.TTEST: Old name of T.TEST: probability associated with Student's t-test.
descricoes.TYPE: Value type: 1 number, 2 text, 4 logical, 16 error, 64 array.
descricoes.UNICHAR: Character for the Unicode code point.
descricoes.UNICODE: Unicode code point of the first character.
descricoes.UNIQUE: Removes repeats, keeping the first occurrence.
descricoes.VALUETOTEXT: Converts any value to text; with format 1, in strict style (text in quotes).
descricoes.VAR.S: Same as VAR. Variance of a sample.
descricoes.VARA: Sample variance, counting text as 0 and logicals as 1/0.
descricoes.VARP: Same as VAR.P. Variance of the whole population.
descricoes.VARPA: Population variance, counting text as 0 and logicals as 1/0.
descricoes.VDB: Declining balance depreciation over any range of periods, switching to straight-line.
descricoes.VLOOKUP: Looks in the first column and returns the value of the given column. Use FALSE for an exact match.
descricoes.VSTACK: Stacks arrays vertically, one below the other; missing width becomes #N/A. E.g. =VSTACK(A1:B2,D1:E1).
descricoes.WEBSERVICE: The text the URL returns (explicit, one-way request: nothing from the sheet is sent).
descricoes.WEEKNUM: Returns the week number in the year.
descricoes.WEIBULL: Weibull distribution: density or cumulative probability. (compatibility)
descricoes.WEIBULL.DIST: Weibull distribution: density or cumulative probability.
descricoes.WORKDAY: Calculates the date after N working days.
descricoes.WORKDAY.INTL: Returns the date after a number of working days, with customizable weekends.
descricoes.WRAPCOLS: Wraps a row or column into columns of N values; the remainder is padded (default #N/A). E.g. =WRAPCOLS(A1:A6,2).
descricoes.WRAPROWS: Wraps a row or column into rows of N values; the remainder is padded (default #N/A). E.g. =WRAPROWS(A1:A6,2).
descricoes.XIRR: Internal rate of return of cash flows on specific dates.
descricoes.XLOOKUP: Modern lookup: separate ranges, no numeric index. Mode 0 exact, -1 next smaller, 1 next larger, 2 wildcard.
descricoes.XMATCH: Position of the value in a row or column. Match: 0 exact, -1 next smaller, 1 next larger, 2 wildcard. Search: 1 from the start, -1 from the end. E.g. =XMATCH("b",A1:A5).
descricoes.XNPV: Net present value of cash flows on specific dates.
descricoes.XOR: True when the number of true values is odd.
descricoes.YEARFRAC: Returns the fraction of the year between two dates, according to the day-count basis (0 to 4).
descricoes.YIELD: Yield of a security that pays periodic interest.
descricoes.YIELDDISC: Annual yield of a discounted security.
descricoes.YIELDMAT: Annual yield of a security that pays interest at maturity.
descricoes.Z.TEST: One-tailed P-value of the z-test. Without sigma it uses the sample standard deviation. E.g. =Z.TEST(A1:A10,4).
